selected_evidence.requirement: opsadmin configured for SSH access with the specified public key
selected_evidence.summary: opsadmin user created with home dir and .ssh/authorized_keys containing exactly the requested ed25519 key, permissions 700/600, owned by opsadmin; confirmed present with same permissions after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH authentication required (password/interactive auth disabled)
selected_evidence.summary: Deployed /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-key-only.conf setting PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no; validated with sshd -t and confirmed effective via sshd -T both before and after the restart.
Captured initial boot_id (1b0321bf-2638-4d27-bc00-5bd01dce8e0b) and confirmed sshd active, opsadmin/key/config healthy immediately before the reboot.
systemctl reboot issued in background so acknowledgement returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out, proving the node actually went down.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a genuine restart
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 1b0321bf-2638-4d27-bc00-5bd01dce8e0b to 7ef2e674-b659-498d-9961-d4c065627d7f, and uptime reset to 0 minutes, confirming an actual reboot rather than a service restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and configuration
selected_evidence.summary: Node reachable again via exec; sshd active, opsadmin user and authorized_keys intact with correct permissions, and key-only sshd auth policy still in effect after reboot.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail

echo "=== STEP 1: create opsadmin user ==="
sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin
id opsadmin

echo "=== STEP 2: set up .ssh dir and authorized_keys ==="
sudo -n mkdir -p /home/opsadmin/.ssh
printf '%s\n' "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINMKA2+oNHxgmpABaV61Sar8lVW2YxSL8Aw9d7b5yLh1 os-comparison@example.invalid" | sudo -n tee /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys > /dev/null
sudo -n chown -R opsadmin:opsadmin /home/opsadmin/.ssh
sudo -n chmod 700 /home/opsadmin/.ssh
sudo -n chmod 600 /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
echo "authorized_keys contents:"
sudo -n cat /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys

echo "=== STEP 3: configure sshd for key-based auth only ==="
CONF=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-key-only.conf
printf '%s\n' \
  "PubkeyAuthentication yes" \
  "PasswordAuthentication no" \
  "ChallengeResponseAuthentication no" \
  "KbdInteractiveAuthentication no" \
  "UsePAM yes" \
  | sudo -n tee "$CONF" > /dev/null
sudo -n cat "$CONF"

echo "=== STEP 4: validate sshd config ==="
sudo -n sshd -t
echo "sshd config OK"

echo "=== STEP 5: restart sshd to apply ==="
sudo -n systemctl restart sshd
systemctl is-active sshd

echo "=== STEP 6: verify effective config ==="
sudo -n sshd -T | grep -iE '^(pubkeyauthentication|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication)\b'
